A garage door: when someone comes within 4 m (on foot or in a car, on either side) it folds up into the garage like a sectional door, about its top edge, and lies under the ceiling; it comes down again when they are gone. It folds towards the side your rooms are on. The export's client/doors.lua moves it; no door script is needed.

A sliding door:when someone comes within 2 m it slides aside (into the wall, towards the side set below) and slides shut when they are gone. A double door opens to both sides at once. The export's client/doors.lua moves it; no door script is needed.

A swing door that opens both ways by itself: when someone comes within 2 m it swings away from them (to the other side of the wall, whichever side they come from) and closes when they are gone, like a kitchen or a café door. A double door opens both leaves. The export's client/doors.lua moves it; no door script is needed.
The game's door: it swings about its hinge when it is pushed, or your door script (ox_doorlock...) moves it.
Double door: two leaves side by side

The width is the whole doorway: each leaf is half of it, hinged on the outer edges (the orange lines) and meeting in the middle where their knobs are (the right leaf is the model mirrored). Each leaf is a door prop of its own for your door script. Turning this on doubles the width (each leaf keeps the size the door had), turning it off halves it.
Seen from the front (the green arrow points to the front): the door slides towards the orange line, by its own width, into the wall.

Seen from the front (the green arrow points to the front); the orange line is the hinge, it starts on the side opposite the knob. The door is a prop of its own that swings about the hinge, with a collision box the thickness of the leaf: your door script (ox_doorlock...) moves it. Its opening in the interior wall is centred on the door, with room each side for the leaf to turn, so it does not catch on the wall.
Also block the doorway with solid collision (it stays when a door script opens the door)

The door prop has its own collision box. If the game gives you no collision there, turn this on: the doorway is blocked by the interior's own collision, which always works, but it stays blocked when the door is swung open.

This door stands in a frame: the frame's hole is the cut in the room's wall, and the door is sized to the frame's opening (the opening less room to swing).

A window frame goes round a window: put it on an opening cut with the Window tool (or press the first button) to make its outside that size. A window you put into it takes the size of its opening (the second button does it again); the window's hole is then the cut in the room's wall. Without a window it is an empty frame with its own hole.

The frame sits in the wall cut and its hole is the cut in the room's wall. Put it over the building's door faces (or press the first button) to make its outside the size of that opening; doors that stand in it are sized to its opening with the second.

The wall cut is centred on the door: the door plus the same gap on each side, enough for the leaf to turn about its hinge. Put the door over the building's door faces (or press the button) to cut the room's wall to the same size as the building's opening, with the door in the middle of it.

The model holds a whole block. Click one building: the others are hidden, the grid is squared to its walls and centered on it, and the camera goes to it. Small parts attached to it (porch, steps) come along. Shift+click adds or removes a part (set "Other buildings" to Ghost to see what else is near). Each building of the project has its own grid, rooms and openings: if the building you are working on already has rooms, clicking a different building starts a new building for it (the first keeps everything). Switch between them in the Buildings list.

Set the grid first. Click a straight wall to turn the grid square to it. Shift+click a wall to put the floor at its bottom edge, Alt+click to move the corner (0, 0) there. A flat floor of the model sets the corner and the floor height in one click. You can also type the numbers in the Import tab.

Drag the blue arrow up or down to raise or lower all the rooms against the model, until the floor matches the building. Ctrl snaps to 5 cm, Shift moves finely, Esc or right-click cancels. Or click a floor of the model to put the rooms' floor at that height. The cutters stay where they are on the model.
Drag a rectangle to add it to the interior (floor, walls, ceiling). Its edges snap to the model's own walls and to 5 cm.
Drag a rectangle to take it out of the interior (a column, a closet).

Green areas are gaps between your rooms (no wider than "Largest gap"). Click one to fill it as part of the interior. Shift+click a closed hole fills it whatever its size. "Fill all" fills every green area.
Drag a straight line to build an interior wall. Doors in it come from the Door tool.

Click the faces of a door on the model (the flat patch under the pointer lights up; Shift: just one triangle), or use Auto-cut to scan named door and window materials. The faces are cut out and the opening is filled with the door model you chose in the Import tab. Delete gives the faces back.

Click the faces of a window on the model (the flat patch under the pointer lights up; Shift: just one triangle), or use Auto-cut to scan named door and window materials. The faces are cut out and the opening is filled with glass. Delete gives the faces back.
Click a wall to cut a wide, tall opening (1.6 x 2.3 m by default) with a box, like a boolean in Blender.

Window and door models from .glb files. Add a .glb to the project (Add .glb models, or drag it onto the window): a file with several windows becomes one model per window. Choose a model in the list and click a wall to put it there, then use the gizmo: drag the coloured arrows to move it along an axis (dragging the model itself slides it along the wall), the cubes on its faces to change its size (Alt: from the middle), the white cube on the corner to scale it all together, the yellow ring to turn it (15 degree steps). Shift = fine / no snapping. R turns it 90 degrees, Shift+R turns it around, Shift+D duplicates, X removes it. Nothing is cut from the building: select the faces behind the model with the button and delete them in the Delete faces tool.

Every prop and plant of the whole model is drawn as its real model. Pick what to show: plants, props, model pieces (vents, pipes). Click selects, Shift+click adds, A selects all, Alt+A none, Ctrl+I inverts, X or Delete removes, R keeps, Ctrl+Z undoes. Props and plants are hidden in the game by a script; model bushes and pieces are taken out of their file. Plants in a room or at a window are removed by default.
Drag a rectangle to give that part of the floor the floor texture chosen in the Paint tab.
Click the floor to hang a ceiling light there. Click a light again to remove it. Only the lights you place are exported.

A person to judge heights against (1.8 m by default). Click the floor to stand the figure there, drag it to move it, R turns it by 45 degrees. It stays in view with the other tools until you remove it. It is only a view aid: it is never saved or exported.

Works like Blender's edit mode: select, then act. Click selects the flat patch under the pointer (Ctrl+click: one triangle, Alt+click: the whole connected piece such as a grille or a vent), Shift+click adds or removes, and dragging draws a box that selects the faces you can see in it (Shift adds, Ctrl takes away). A selects all, Alt+A none, Ctrl+I inverts, L selects the piece under the pointer, Ctrl+L grows the selection to whole pieces, Shift+G selects everything with the same texture. X or Delete deletes the selection (Ctrl+Z brings it back). Use it for fake doors, painted-on windows, details that stick out and solid wall pieces. Turn on "Detail models" to reach the grilles, vents and bushes: they are separate files that go with the building and are changed in the export too. Deleting can leave a hole in a wall: the Edges tool fills it.

Every model is made of parts: all the faces that share one texture. Click a part in the view, or a row in the list, to see it; Remove takes every face of it out of the model and out of the export, Restore gives them back. Use it for whole textures (decals, a window page, a detail file); for single pieces use Delete faces.

The building's collision is what stops you in the game, and you cannot see it. The orange lines are its pieces (triangles and boxes) around your rooms. Click one to select it, Shift+click adds or removes, drag a box to select the pieces inside it (Shift adds, Ctrl takes away), A selects all, Alt+A none, Ctrl+I inverts, Shift+G the same material, X or Delete deletes the selection (Ctrl+Z brings it back). The three collision files of a building overlap, so a deleted piece takes the piece of about the same size at the same place in the other files with it (switch that off below). Rooms are already cleared of collision; use this for what is left, or for collision outside them (frames, ledges, props).

Collision you build yourself, for what has to stop you but has none (a ledge or step of the model whose collision you deleted, a railing, a counter). Drag on the floor to draw a box (on a ledge or step of the model it stands on that surface); the first box is 1 m tall, the height is set with the stem on top, or by typing it. Tests the collision the game will have, before you go there. A player-sized capsule (set its width, height and step below) is put on the floor of the biggest room and walked everywhere it fits. It uses the interior's own collision (walls, floor, door frames, window glass), your collision boxes and what is left of the building's collision after the export's cuts. It finds: parts of the rooms it cannot reach, doorways it cannot pass (and what blocks them), gaps in the walls it can walk out through, pieces of the building's collision standing in your rooms, holes in the floor and boxes that float. Click the floor to start the walk somewhere else. Click a line of the result to see where it is. Green is where the player can stand, orange is closed off, red is an invisible piece of the building, pink is a hole. The door model itself is not part of this (it is a prop with its own collision that your door script moves).

Nothing is built for you. "Whole new building": build on a grid like a house builder (rooms, doors, windows, stairs, levels, roof). Either way Export writes a FiveM resource folder you upload to your server.
